content: The generation-1 scan has closed the lead I inherited. Ten C4 substituents spanning every electronic class land between 0.51 and 0.61: trifluoromethyl and methylamino both hit 0.61 despite being opposite in electronics, bromine 0.60, ethynyl 0.59, propynyl 0.58, iodine 0.57, methylthio and acetyl 0.56. Against methyl at 0.49 and fluorine at 0.53, the reading is that C4 wants to be occupied by something larger than a methyl or a small halogen and is close to indifferent about what. So jnk3 is capped near 0.61 and QED is the binding constraint again - and bromine wins not because it is the most active but because it is the only group that is active without costing drug-likeness. Ligand 1 is the acetyl probe; atom 17 is its cyclopropane CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 15, the anchor that holds the best cap. The nitrile is the one strong candidate never paired with it: 0.58 on a cyclobutyl cap, and it is 54 Da lighter and much less lipophilic than bromine, so on a cyclopropyl it should post a high QED. Expected product: about 292 Da.
